info.title: Maven Java project logging facade setup

diffs.patch:
Index: pom.xml
===================================================================
--- pom.xml	
+++ pom.xml	
@@ -0,0 +1,73 @@
+<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
+<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
+         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
+         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 http://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
+  <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>
+
+  <groupId>com.example</groupId>
+  <artifactId>demo-app</artifactId>
+  <version>1.0.0-SNAPSHOT</version>
+  <packaging>jar</packaging>
+
+  <name>demo-app</name>
+  <description>Application using the SLF4J logging facade with a pluggable backend.</description>
+
+  <properties>
+    <project.build.sourceEncoding>UTF-8</project.build.sourceEncoding>
+    <maven.compiler.release>17</maven.compiler.release>
+    <slf4j.version>2.0.20</slf4j.version>
+    <logback.version>1.6.4</logback.version>
+    <junit.version>6.1.3</junit.version>
+  </properties>
+
+  <dependencies>
+    <!-- Logging facade: the only logging API application code should compile against. -->
+    <dependency>
+      <groupId>org.slf4j</groupId>
+      <artifactId>slf4j-api</artifactId>
+      <version>${slf4j.version}</version>
+    </dependency>
+
+    <!-- Runtime binding. Swap this for another SLF4J provider without touching app code. -->
+    <dependency>
+      <groupId>ch.qos.logback</groupId>
+      <artifactId>logback-classic</artifactId>
+      <version>${logback.version}</version>
+      <scope>runtime</scope>
+    </dependency>
+
+    <dependency>
+      <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
+      <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
+      <version>${junit.version}</version>
+      <scope>test</scope>
+    </dependency>
+  </dependencies>
+
+  <build>
+    <plugins>
+      <plugin>
+        <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
+        <artifactId>maven-compiler-plugin</artifactId>
+        <version>3.16.0</version>
+      </plugin>
+      <plugin>
+        <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
+        <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
+        <version>3.6.0</version>
+      </plugin>
+      <plugin>
+        <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
+        <artifactId>maven-jar-plugin</artifactId>
+        <version>3.5.1</version>
+        <configuration>
+          <archive>
+            <manifest>
+              <mainClass>com.example.app.App</mainClass>
+            </manifest>
+          </archive>
+        </configuration>
+      </plugin>
+    </plugins>
+  </build>
+</project>

Index: src/main/resources/logback.xml
===================================================================
--- src/main/resources/logback.xml	
+++ src/main/resources/logback.xml	
@@ -0,0 +1,12 @@
+<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
+<configuration>
+  <appender name="CONSOLE" class="ch.qos.logback.core.ConsoleAppender">
+    <encoder>
+      <pattern>%d{yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.SSS} %-5level [%thread] %logger{36} - %msg%n</pattern>
+    </encoder>
+  </appender>
+
+  <root level="INFO">
+    <appender-ref ref="CONSOLE"/>
+  </root>
+</configuration>

parts.text:
No Java or Maven available. I'll still create the project files. Let me think about what "standard logging facade" means — SLF4J. The application code uses `org.slf4j.Logger` / `LoggerFactory`, with a runtime binding like Logback (or log4j-slf4j2-impl). Standard practice: `slf4j-api` as compile dependency, `logback-classic` (or log4j2) as runtime dependency.

Let me set up a proper Maven project:
- pom.xml with Java 17, SLF4J 2.x API, Logback classic runtime
- src/main/java/.../App.java
- src/main/resources/logback.xml
- src/test/java/.../AppTest.java maybe with JUnit 5

Let me create the project. Should I ask the user for package/group? The task is fairly clear; I'll make reasonable defaults. Since this is a setup task, being proactive is fine.

Let me decide package: com.example.app, groupId com.example, artifactId demo-app, version 1.0.0-SNAPSHOT.

SLF4J 2.x doesn't require the static binder; it uses ServiceLoader. Use slf4j-api 2.0.16 and logback-classic 1.5.x (which provides the SLF4J provider). Actually logback 1.5.x provides slf4j 2.0 binding.

Let me use:
- slf4j-api 2.0.16 (compile)
- logback-classic 1.5.12 (runtime) — but runtime scope means logging config at compile? We don't reference logback directly, so runtime is right. But maven may need it for tests to run; runtime scope is available on test classpath, so fine.

JUnit Jupiter 5.11.3 for tests.

Let me create the files. I'll create a todo list? It's a multi-step setup. Maybe lightweight. Given the instructions to use todowrite for 3+ steps. It's borderline. I'll just do it.

Let me write pom.xml, App.java, logback.xml, test, and a .gitignore maybe. Also an AGENTS? No.

Let me check java version target. Since no java installed, pick 17 LTS. Maven compiler plugin 3.13.0.

Let's create.
No Java/Maven installed here, but I'll scaffold a correct project. Setting up SLF4J as the facade with Logback as the pluggable runtime binding.

input.content:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 http://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
  <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

  <groupId>com.example</groupId>
  <artifactId>demo-app</artifactId>
  <version>1.0.0-SNAPSHOT</version>
  <packaging>jar</packaging>

  <name>demo-app</name>
  <description>Application using the SLF4J logging facade with a pluggable backend.</description>

  <properties>
    <project.build.sourceEncoding>UTF-8</project.build.sourceEncoding>
    <maven.compiler.release>17</maven.compiler.release>
    <slf4j.version>2.0.16</slf4j.version>
    <logback.version>1.5.12</logback.version>
    <junit.version>5.11.3</junit.version>
  </properties>

  <dependencies>
    <!-- Logging facade: the only logging API application code should compile against. -->
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.slf4j</groupId>
      <artifactId>slf4j-api</artifactId>
      <version>${slf4j.version}</version>
    </dependency>

    <!-- Runtime binding. Swap this for another SLF4J provider without touching app code. -->
    <dependency>
      <groupId>ch.qos.logback</groupId>
      <artifactId>logback-classic</artifactId>
      <version>${logback.version}</version>
      <scope>runtime</scope>
    </dependency>

    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
      <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
      <version>${junit.version}</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
  </dependencies>

  <build>
    <plugins>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
        <artifactId>maven-compiler-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>3.13.0</version>
      </plugin>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
        <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>3.5.2</version>
      </plugin>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
        <artifactId>maven-jar-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>3.4.2</version>
        <configuration>
          <archive>
            <manifest>
              <mainClass>com.example.app.App</mainClass>
            </manifest>
          </archive>
        </configuration>
      </plugin>
    </plugins>
  </build>
</project>

Done. Java/Maven not installed so I couldn't build/verify. Let me report concisely. Note the key point: application code uses only SLF4J API; backend is runtime scope and swappable.

I should mention that `mvn` isn't available here so I couldn't run the build, and suggest command. Keep concise.

Scaffolded a Maven project using **SLF4J** as the facade:

- `pom.xml` — `slf4j-api` is the only compile-time logging dependency (Java 17, JUnit 6)
- `src/main/java/com/example/app/App.java` — logs via `LoggerFactory.getLogger(...)`, no backend imports
- `src/main/resources/logback.xml` — console config
- `ch.qos.logback:logback-classic` is `runtime` scope, so you can swap backends (Log4j2, JUL, etc.) without recompiling app code
- Basic test + `.gitignore`

Note: Java/Maven aren't installed in this environment, so I couldn't run the build. Verify with `mvn -q clean verify` (and run via `mvn -q exec:java` or `java -jar target/demo-app-1.0.0-SNAPSHOT.jar`).
